title.narrative: Haiti ACJR 2025

description.narrative: Hurricane Melissa has dramatically worsened Haiti’s already complex humanitarian crisis, with Grand’Anse among the departments most severely affected. Between the 23rd -29th October, torrential rains, flooding, and landslides have devastated the area. Grand’Anse has suffered widespread destruction and significant losses to agriculture, infrastructure, and livelihoods. Its capital, Jérémie, is one of the most affected communes in the country, with 2,890 HH displaced housed in schools and churches, equivalent to approximately 22,542 people (ACTED RNA Oct 2025). Pre-crisis levels of food insecurity were already among the highest in the country; 94% of households reported insufficient food consumption. Post-disaster assessments indicate a further deterioration, with up to 75% of families now eating one meal or less, and crop losses estimated at up to 90% of local production. As of June 2025, nearly 1.3 million people were internally displaced, the highest figure ever recorded in Haiti. While Hurricane Melissa itself has caused acute needs in Grand’Anse in particular in FSL, Shelter and WASH, Haiti's ongoing crisis remains very much a protection crisis.

Plan and CAPAC propose an intervention that combines MPC (to cover basic needs incl. FSL and shelter), WASH (primarily to combat cholera and ensure access to clean water) as well as Protection including case management and MHPSS levels 1-3 (to address the ongoing and now escalated Protection crisis).

SUMMARY The intervention targets three communal sections of Grand’Anse: Basse-Voldrogue, Fond Rouge Dahère, and Fond Rouge Torbeck. Plan and CAPAC will deliver a multi-sectoral, child-centred response focusing on WASH, MPC, and CP through child-friendly spaces and direct community interventions. Activities include hygiene promotion, distribution of water and hygiene kits, and integrated protection messaging. CFS will serve as safe hubs for cash assistance, psychosocial support, and information on protection and health, including GBV and cholera prevention.
Plan will rehabilitate one CFS per section, provide CP case management, and establish referral pathways to health, GBV, and legal services. CAPAC, with Plan’s technical support, will deliver MPC to meet urgent needs for NFIs, shelter, and healthcare, prioritizing vulnerable families identified through CP and CFS activities.

The intervention targets three communal sections of Grand’Anse: Basse-Voldrogue, Fond Rouge Dahère, and Fond Rouge Torbeck. Plan and CAPAC will implement a child-centred, multi-sectoral response focusing on WASH, MPC, and CP through child-friendly spaces and direct community activities. Plan will lead WASH interventions, including hygiene promotion sessions, distribution of water and hygiene kits, and integration of protection and preparedness messages. Volunteers will receive incentives for 3months to maintain sanitary latrines in overcrowded shelters. CAPAC, with technical support from Plan, will provide multipurpose cash assistance to meet urgent needs for NFIs, shelter, and healthcare, prioritizing highly vulnerable families identified through CP and CFS activities. MPC will help families cover essential needs and reduce protection risks. To address increased protection concerns and psychosocial distress, Plan will rehabilitate one CFS per section, deliver play-based PSS, manage CP cases, and establish referral pathways to health, GBV, and legal services. CFS will serve as safe hubs for cash assistance, psychosocial support, and information on protection topics such as PSHEA, GBV, and cholera prevention.

The project will target displaced families in Grand’Anse, one of the departments most affected by Hurricane Melissa, where flooding and destruction have forced thousands into temporary shelters and severely disrupted access to basic services. Priority will be given to female-headed households, children, and other at-risk groups.

WASH Distribution of 600 hygiene kits to vulnerable households, reaching about 3,000 people. Each kit includes laundry and bathing soap, toothpaste and toothbrush, toilet paper, sanitary pads, Aquatabs, and a 20L bucket with lid and tap for safe water storage. Kits are designed according to UNICEF WASH standards and ensure inclusion of women and persons with disabilities. Community hygiene awareness sessions on handwashing, safe water use, and prevention of waterborne diseases will be conducted in three communal sections of Jérémie, reaching around 8,403 people. Activities will use participatory methods and ensure inclusion of women, youth, and persons with disabilities.
Protection 6,563 people will benefit from community awareness sessions on child protection and GBV, psychosocial support in child-friendly spaces, and follow-up of cases identified through the case management system. Individual case management for 150 children with urgent protection needs, including identification, assessment, referral, and follow-up to specialized services. All actions will ensure confidentiality, gender sensitivity, and coordination with local protection actors.
MPC Provision of multipurpose cash assistance to 900 vulnerable households, reaching approximately 4,500 people. Transfers will support essential needs such as food, non-food items, shelter, and healthcare. Delivery will be secure through financial service providers and coordinated with local authorities to ensure transparency and accountability.
